intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with nearly 1,500 years of history, followed by a visit to the stunning Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque) just across the square. Marvel at Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman architecture, and the spiritual atmosphere of one of the world's greatest monuments.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Immersion
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and aromatic spices. Engage with local vendors, practice bargaining, and soak in centuries of trading culture.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Ottoman History Deep Dive
experiences.description: Explore the sprawling Topkapi Palace complex, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Visit the Imperial Treasury, Harem quarters, sacred relics, and enjoy panoramic views of the Bosphorus. Combine with a stop at the adjacent Istanbul Archaeology Museums for a full day of Ottoman and ancient history.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Breakfast & Bosphorus Ferry Cruise
experiences.description: Start the day with an authentic Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) featuring olives, white cheese, simit, eggs, honey, and çay at a local tea house in Karaköy. Afterward, board a public Bosphorus ferry for a scenic cruise between Europe and Asia, passing Ottoman palaces, waterfront mansions (yalıs), and historic fortresses at a fraction of tourist cruise prices.

experiences.name: Balık Ekmek, Meyhane Dinner & Istiklal Street Night Walk
experiences.description: Begin the evening with a famous balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the floating boats near Galata Bridge, a beloved Istanbul street food tradition. Then explore the lively Beyoğlu neighborhood, dine at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) in Nevizade Sokak with meze platters and rakı, and stroll the vibrant Istiklal Avenue with its historic tram, music, and street performers.
experiences.location: Galata Bridge, Nevizade Sokak & Istiklal Avenue, Beyoğlu

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or metro to minimize transfer costs (approx. 50-70 TRY vs. 400-600 TRY for a taxi). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack near the hotel — look for a 24-hour büfe (corner shop) or döner stand for a cheap wrap (30-50 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night simple. Download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline) and get a local SIM card at the airport (Turkcell or Vodafone Turkey) for data — around 150-200 TRY for 10GB. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel. Walk along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings. Head to a local simit cart for breakfast — a classic Istanbul street breakfast of simit (sesame bread ring) with tea costs under 20 TRY.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take public transport (tram or bus) toward the Old City (Sultanahmet). Visit the Hippodrome of Constantinople (free), the German Fountain, and the Egyptian Obelisk. Stroll through the surrounding historic streets and soak in the atmosphere. Visit the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — entry is free but check prayer times.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Sultanahmet neighborhood at dusk when the mosques are beautifully lit. Head back toward your hotel area and find a local lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) for dinner — these serve home-cooked meals at very affordable prices.

meals.breakfast: Simit and çay (tea) from a street cart near the hotel — 15-25 TRY
meals.lunch: Börek (savory pastry) from a local bakery in Sultanahmet — 40-60 TRY
meals.dinner: Lokanta dinner near hotel — lentil soup, bread, and a main dish for 80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Buy an Istanbul Kart (transit card) today — costs about 100 TRY deposit and saves significant money on all public transport. Single rides with the card are around 15-20 TRY vs. 40+ TRY with cash.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (Ayasofya) — now a mosque but open to visitors outside prayer times, free entry. Arrive early (before 9am) to avoid crowds. Marvel at the breathtaking Byzantine architecture, mosaics, and massive dome. Dress modestly and women should bring a headscarf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Topkapi Palace — entry fee around 500-600 TRY but absolutely worth it for history lovers. Explore the courtyards, treasury, and harem (separate ticket ~300 TRY). This was the administrative center of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Gulhane Park (free) adjacent to Topkapi for sunset views of the Bosphorus. Head to the Eminonu waterfront for a famous fish sandwich (balik ekmek) from the floating boats — a beloved Istanbul street food for about 60-80 TRY.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at a neighborhood café near hotel — eggs, cheese, olives, tomatoes, bread, tea for 80-120 TRY
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a quick gözleme (stuffed flatbread) from a street vendor near Topkapi — 50-70 TRY
meals.dinner: Balik ekmek (fish sandwich) and ayran at Eminonu waterfront — 80-100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Museum Pass Istanbul (around 1,200 TRY) covers multiple major museums and may save money if you plan to visit 3+ paid sites. Calculate based on your planned visits. Topkapi is a full-day site — pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapali Çarsi) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, free to enter. Open from around 9am. Browse the 4,000+ shops selling spices, textiles, ceramics, jewelry, and souvenirs. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are always negotiable. Start at 50% of the asking price.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Spice Bazaar (Misir Çarsisi) — also free to enter. Buy local spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and nuts. This is a great place to pick up affordable, authentic gifts. Then explore the surrounding Eminonu and Tahtakale neighborhood markets.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot (free) — watch local fishermen lining the bridge railings. Head up to the Beyoglu district. Walk up Istiklal Avenue, Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard, and enjoy the street performers and historic tram.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local café — 60-80 TRY
meals.lunch: Kuru fasulye (white bean stew) and rice at a traditional lokanta near the Grand Bazaar — 70-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Lahmacun (Turkish flatbread pizza) and ayran at a Beyoglu street restaurant — 60-80 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Don't buy from the very first stall in the Grand Bazaar — prices are highest there. Wander deeper inside for better deals. Be cautious of carpet shop invitations that seem overly friendly — they often lead to high-pressure sales.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnici) — an underground Byzantine water storage chamber with atmospheric lighting and ancient columns. Entry around 300-400 TRY. Nearby, visit the small but fascinating Mosaic Museum (part of the Great Palace of Constantinople) — check Museum Pass coverage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arasta Bazaar (free to browse) behind the Blue Mosque — less touristy than the Grand Bazaar with quality crafts. Then visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts near the Hippodrome — entry around 200-300 TRY, featuring carpets, calligraphy, and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free sound and light show at the Hippodrome area (seasonal — check schedule). Walk through the quieter backstreets of Sultanahmet and discover neighborhood tea houses (çay bahçesi) where locals play backgammon. Join for a glass of tea for 10-15 TRY.

meals.breakfast: Simit, boiled egg, and tea from a street cart — 25-35 TRY
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at a local çorba salonu (soup restaurant) near Sultanahmet — 50-70 TRY
meals.dinner: Pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a neighborhood pide restaurant — 100-150 TRY for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern was recently renovated and is stunning. Book online in advance to avoid queues. The area around Sultanahmet has many tourist-trap restaurants — walk one or two streets away from the main square for much better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry from Eminonu to Kadikoy on the Asian side of Istanbul — one of the best and cheapest experiences in the city (single fare ~20 TRY with Istanbul Kart). The 20-minute Bosphorus crossing offers stunning views of the skyline. Explore the vibrant Kadikoy market neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Kadikoy Produce Market (Kadikoy Pazari) — a colorful local market selling fresh produce, fish, cheese, olives, and street food. Visit the Moda neighborhood, a charming residential area with cafés and sea views. Walk along the Moda coastline for free Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kadikoy's nightlife street (Kadife Sokak, known as Bar Street) for the atmosphere. Have dinner in Kadikoy where prices are generally lower than the tourist-heavy European side. Take the ferry back to Eminonu after dinner for more Bosphorus night views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or a simit from the ferry terminal — 15-25 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh meze and grilled fish at a Kadikoy market restaurant — 120-180 TRY
meals.dinner: Kokoreç (grilled offal sandwich — adventurous but authentic!) or köfte at a Kadikoy street spot — 60-90 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Kadikoy is a fantastic contrast to the tourist-heavy European side — more local, younger vibe, great food scene. The ferry ride itself IS the attraction. Use your Istanbul Kart for the ferry to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — one of the finest examples of Byzantine mosaic art in the world. Take bus or tram to reach it. Entry around 200-300 TRY. The mosaics depicting the life of Christ and Virgin Mary are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls (free) — the 5th-century land walls that protected Constantinople for 1,000 years. Explore the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — historic Jewish and Greek quarters with colorful houses, antique shops, and a very authentic atmosphere. These neighborhoods are Instagram-worthy and completely free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Fatih neighborhood for a very local, budget-friendly dinner experience. Visit a traditional Turkish bath (hamam) for an evening — Çemberlitas Hamam or Cagaloglu Hamam are historic options (400-600 TRY for a basic wash and scrub).

meals.breakfast: Menemen or borek at a Balat neighborhood café — 70-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Tantuni (spiced meat wrap) from a local street stall in Fatih — 50-70 TRY
meals.dinner: Fatih lokanta dinner — hearty traditional Turkish dishes for 80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Balat is very photogenic with its colorful houses — go in the morning or afternoon for best light. The neighborhood is gentrifying but still very authentic. Wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestone and hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) in Beyoglu — one of Istanbul's most iconic landmarks. Entry around 300-400 TRY. The tower offers 360-degree panoramic views of Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and Golden Horn. Arrive early to avoid crowds. The surrounding Galata neighborhood has charming streets worth exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up Istiklal Avenue from Galata to Taksim Square. Visit the historic Cicek Pasaji (Flower Passage) and the covered Balik Pazari (Fish Market) for free browsing. Explore the side streets of Beyoglu — Asmalimescit and Nevizade streets are famous for meyhane (tavern) culture. Visit the Pera Museum if interested in Ottoman-era paintings (entry ~200 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Experience a meyhane dinner in Beyoglu — these traditional Turkish taverns serve meze (small dishes) and raki (anise spirit). Go with a group to share costs. Look for set menus around 200-300 TRY per person including food and one drink.

meals.breakfast: Açik büfe (open buffet) at a Beyoglu café — 100-150 TRY
meals.lunch: Midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from a street vendor on Istiklal — 5-7 TRY each, eat 10-15 for a filling snack
meals.dinner: Meyhane meze dinner in Nevizade — 200-300 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Midye dolma (stuffed mussels) are a quintessential Istanbul street food — the vendor will squeeze lemon on each one. Only buy from vendors with high turnover to ensure freshness. Beyoglu is very walkable — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry cruise — the public ferry from Eminonu to Anadolu Kavagi (the last stop on the Asian side) is one of Istanbul's best budget experiences. The full round trip takes about 6 hours total and costs only the ferry fare (~40-60 TRY each way with Istanbul Kart). Enjoy views of palaces, fortresses, and mansions along the shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Anadolu Kavagi village — a charming fishing village at the mouth of the Black Sea. Hike up to the ruined Yoros Castle (free) for spectacular views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. The village has many fresh fish restaurants — this is a great splurge opportunity.
day_by_day.evening: Take the return ferry back to Eminonu as the sun sets over the city — the views are spectacular. This is one of the most memorable experiences in Istanbul and costs almost nothing. Arrive back at Eminonu by evening.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from a simit cart before boarding the ferry — 20-30 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at Anadolu Kavagi — this is a worthwhile splurge (200-300 TRY for a full fish meal)
meals.dinner: Light dinner back near the hotel — soup and bread at a local place — 60-80 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (BUDO/Sehir Hatlari) is NOT the same as the tourist cruise boats — it's much cheaper and more authentic. Check the ferry schedule at Eminonu in advance as boats run at set times. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Muzesi) near Topkapi Palace — one of the world's great archaeology museums with artifacts from across the former Ottoman Empire. Entry around 300-400 TRY. Highlights include the Alexander Sarcophagus and the Treaty of Kadesh. The complex also includes the Tiled Kiosk (Cinili Kosk) with magnificent Iznik tiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sirkeci neighborhood — historically the end point of the Orient Express. Visit Sirkeci Train Station (free, still operational) with its beautiful Orientalist architecture. Walk along the Golden Horn waterfront. Visit the Rahmi M. Koç Museum on the Golden Horn if interested in industrial history (entry ~200 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Karakoy neighborhood — a hip, revitalized waterfront area with great street art, cafés, and the famous Karakoy Güllüoglu baklava shop. Try fresh baklava here — it's considered among the best in Istanbul (50-100 TRY for a portion). Walk across the Galata Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast spread at a Sirkeci café — 100-130 TRY
meals.lunch: Kumpir (loaded baked potato) from a street vendor — 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Karakoy meyhane or taverna — meze and main for 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Archaeological Museum is genuinely world-class and often overlooked by tourists focused on Topkapi and Hagia Sophia. Allow at least 2-3 hours. The Tiled Kiosk is included in the same ticket and is a hidden gem.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take the ferry from Kabatas or Eminonu to Buyukada (the largest island). Ferry takes about 90 minutes and costs ~50-70 TRY each way. No cars are allowed on the island — rent a bicycle (100-150 TRY/day) or take a horse-drawn carriage. Explore the Victorian-era wooden mansions and Greek Orthodox monastery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or walk around Buyukada island — visit Aya Yorgi Church on the hilltop for panoramic sea views (free, with a small donation). Swim at one of the small beaches if weather permits (free public beaches available). The island has a peaceful, old-world atmosphere completely different from the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon/evening. Enjoy sunset views of the Istanbul skyline from the ferry. Have dinner near the hotel — you'll be tired from the day trip so keep it simple and local.

meals.breakfast: Eat at hotel or grab simit before catching the ferry — 20-30 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a Buyukada restaurant — 150-250 TRY (reasonable for the island)
meals.dinner: Simple lokanta dinner near hotel — 80-100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance — ferries to the Princes' Islands can be crowded on weekends. The last ferry back to the city is usually in the evening. Buyukada is the most popular island; alternatively visit smaller Heybeliada for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahce Palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapi as the imperial residence. Entry around 600-800 TRY (guided tours only). The palace has 285 rooms, 43 halls, and a 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier. Book in advance. Alternatively, enjoy the free exterior and gardens along the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a tram to the Besiktas neighborhood — a lively, local district with a famous fish market and great street food. Visit the Besiktas market area and explore the neighborhood. Head to Ortakoy — a charming waterfront village with the iconic Ortakoy Mosque set against the Bosphorus Bridge backdrop. Try kumpir (stuffed baked potato) — Ortakoy is famous for it.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset at Ortakoy waterfront — one of the most scenic spots in Istanbul with views of the illuminated Bosphorus Bridge. Have dinner at one of the Ortakoy waterfront restaurants or grab street food from the market stalls. Walk along the Bosphorus promenade.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel or a Besiktas café — 100-130 TRY
meals.lunch: Ortakoy kumpir (stuffed baked potato loaded with toppings) — 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Grilled meat at a Besiktas ocakbasi (grill restaurant) — 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahce Palace requires a guided tour and has timed entry — book online to avoid disappointment. The palace is genuinely opulent but the ticket price is higher than other sites. If budget is tight, skip the interior and enjoy the free waterfront views of the exterior.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit your favorite neighborhood or spot for a leisurely farewell. Visit any remaining sites on your list. Do final souvenir shopping at the Grand Bazaar or Spice Market. Good budget souvenirs: Turkish tea sets, small evil eye (nazar boncugu) amulets, spices, and lokum (Turkish delight).
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a final Turkish lunch at your favorite lokanta. Pack and check out of the hotel. Head to a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden) for a final glass of çay and reflect on your Istanbul journey. If time allows, take one last walk along the Bosphorus waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure time, head to the airport. Take the Havaist bus or metro to keep transport costs low. Enjoy a final börek or simit at the airport as a last taste of Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at a neighborhood spot — 100-150 TRY as a farewell treat
meals.lunch: Final lokanta meal — kuru fasulye, pilav, and salad — 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport food or pack snacks from the Spice Market for the journey — 50-100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. The Havaist bus from various city points takes 45-90 minutes depending on traffic. Keep some Turkish Lira for final transport but exchange remaining currency back before leaving or spend it at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or a nearby 24-hour kebab shop such as a local 'büfe' (Turkish convenience eatery) — try a simple döner wrap or simit with tea to wind down after the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance to avoid taxi hassles at night. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport or use an ATM. Istanbul uses Turkish Lira (TRY). Get a good night's rest — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Ease into Istanbul with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Afterward, take a short orientation walk along the Beachfront promenade near the resort to get your bearings and enjoy the fresh sea breeze over the Bosphorus or Marmara shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Kadıköy neighborhood (if on the Asian side) or explore the Bosphorus waterfront. Visit a local bazaar or street market to get a feel for everyday Istanbul life. Browse fresh produce stalls, spice vendors, and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a traditional meyhane (Turkish tavern) near the hotel. Sample classic meze dishes such as haydari (yogurt dip), sigara böreği (cheese pastry rolls), and grilled fish.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the hotel — cheeses, olives, tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, honey, and fresh bread with çay (tea).
meals.lunch: Casual bite at a local pide (Turkish flatbread) restaurant — try a classic kaşarlı pide (cheese pide) for around 80–120 TRY.
meals.dinner: Meyhane dinner with meze and grilled fish — budget around 300–450 TRY per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day. Use it to recover from jet lag, pick up a local SIM card or activate an eSIM, and download offline maps. Confirm any upcoming tour bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry or metro to the Old City (Sultanahmet). Begin at the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — arrive early to beat crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at its Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and Ottoman additions. Entry is free but dress modestly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 5 minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — admire its stunning six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Then explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople, the ancient chariot racing track, and its monuments including the Obelisk of Theodosius.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet. Visit the Arasta Bazaar for quality souvenirs without aggressive haggling. Enjoy dinner at a rooftop restaurant with views of the illuminated Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish lentil soup (mercimek çorbası) and gözleme (stuffed flatbread) at a local Sultanahmet eatery — around 100–150 TRY.
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Sultanahmet — try Ottoman-style lamb dishes or stuffed eggplant (İmam Bayıldı) — budget 350–500 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking on cobblestones. Women should carry a headscarf for mosque visits. The Blue Mosque closes during prayer times (roughly 5 times daily for 30–90 minutes), so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapı Palace — the heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem complex, and the stunning palace courtyards with Bosphorus views. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to Gülhane Park for a peaceful stroll among rose gardens. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums — three museums in one complex featuring ancient artifacts from across the Ottoman Empire, including Alexander the Great's sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Grand Bazaar area for an evening wander through its surrounding streets. Dine at a historic lokanta (traditional Turkish restaurant) in the Beyazıt neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Packed börek or simit purchased from a street vendor near Gülhane Park — budget 40–70 TRY for a quick, authentic snack.
meals.dinner: Traditional lokanta dinner — choose from daily home-cooked dishes displayed behind glass counters (fasulye, etli güveç, pilav) — budget 150–250 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapı Palace charges separate entry for the Harem — buy a combined ticket at the gate (approximately 500–700 TRY). The Archaeological Museums are an underrated gem — don't skip them. Closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Wander through its labyrinthine lanes, admire handwoven carpets, gold jewelry, ceramics, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Buy local spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and nuts. Afterward, take a short Bosphorus ferry ride from Eminönü — a scenic and affordable way to see the city from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — Sinan's masterpiece perched on Istanbul's highest hill. Enjoy panoramic city views from the mosque courtyard at sunset. Dine in the charming restaurants clustered around the mosque.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the famous floating boats at Eminönü waterfront — an iconic Istanbul street food experience, around 60–80 TRY.
meals.dinner: Dinner near Süleymaniye Mosque — try a traditional Turkish restaurant serving slow-cooked lamb or chicken dishes — budget 250–400 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. The Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar costs just a few TRY using an Istanbulkart (transit card) — highly recommended to get one if you haven't already.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the European side's Beyoğlu district. Walk up the famous İstiklal Avenue — a 1.4 km pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European-style buildings, cafes, bookshops, and galleries. Ride the historic Tünel funicular, one of the world's oldest underground railways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Galata Tower — climb to the top for breathtaking 360-degree views of Istanbul, the Golden Horn, and the Bosphorus. Then explore the charming Galata and Karaköy neighborhoods, known for their hip cafes, street art, and design shops.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Istanbul's vibrant nightlife with a rooftop bar drink in Beyoğlu. Then enjoy dinner at a trendy modern Turkish restaurant in Karaköy — the city's up-and-coming culinary hub.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a classic Beyoğlu pastane (patisserie) — try a fresh börek, poğaça, and Turkish coffee — budget 80–120 TRY.
meals.lunch: Meşhur Dönerci or a well-regarded kebab spot on a side street off İstiklal — budget 120–180 TRY.
meals.dinner: Modern Anatolian cuisine restaurant in Karaköy — budget 400–600 TRY per person for a more elevated dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue can get very crowded, especially on weekends. The nostalgic red tram runs along the avenue and is fun to ride. Galata Tower entry fee is approximately 200–300 TRY — book online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full Bosphorus cruise — book a half-day tour departing from Eminönü or Beşiktaş. Sail past magnificent Ottoman palaces, fortresses, waterfront mansions (yalıs), and the iconic Bosphorus Bridge. This is one of Istanbul's most memorable experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı (the last stop on the long Bosphorus cruise) and hike up to the ruined Yoros Castle for stunning views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Browse the small fishing village's seafood restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the city center. Unwind with a traditional Turkish bath (hammam) experience — try a mid-range hammam in the Sultanahmet or Beyoğlu area for a full scrub and foam massage.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch in Anadolu Kavağı village — grilled sea bass or calamari with salad — budget 250–400 TRY per person.
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the hammam — try a manti (Turkish dumplings) restaurant or a simple pide house — budget 150–250 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (İDO/Şehir Hatları) is the most affordable option (around 50–80 TRY) and runs on a set schedule. Private tour boats are more flexible but pricier. Book the hammam in advance — Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Çağaloğlu Hamamı are historic and mid-range priced (400–700 TRY).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Asian side of Istanbul — take the ferry to Üsküdar. Visit the charming Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) on its tiny island just offshore. Then wander through Üsküdar's traditional neighborhood with its beautiful mosques and local atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kadıköy — Istanbul's most vibrant Asian-side neighborhood. Explore the Kadıköy Market (Moda bazaar area) with its fishmongers, cheese shops, delis, and street food stalls. Browse the bohemian boutiques and vintage shops of Moda district.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Kadıköy — the neighborhood is known for its excellent and affordable food scene. Then catch a live music performance at one of the many meyhanes or music venues in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Street food tour of Kadıköy Market — sample kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), fresh juice, and Turkish pastries — budget 100–150 TRY total.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded Kadıköy meyhane — fish, meze, and raki — budget 300–500 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Maiden's Tower has a cafe/restaurant inside — coffee with a view is lovely. Kadıköy is a favorite among locals and expats — very authentic and less touristy. The ferry between Eminönü and Kadıköy is frequent and scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace that served as the administrative center of the late empire. Marvel at its 285 rooms, 44 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier. Guided tours run approximately 90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Beşiktaş and Ortaköy neighborhoods along the Bosphorus. Visit the picturesque Ortaköy Mosque right on the waterfront. Browse the Sunday artisan market in Ortaköy Square (if applicable) and enjoy the vibrant café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset walk along the Bosphorus promenade from Ortaköy toward Bebek — one of Istanbul's most scenic and exclusive waterfront stretches. Dine at a Bebek waterfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Ortaköy's famous kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato) from a street stall — a local institution, budget 80–120 TRY.
meals.dinner: Waterfront fish restaurant in Bebek or Ortaköy — fresh catch of the day with Bosphorus views — budget 400–600 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Entry fees are around 500–700 TRY. Cameras are not allowed inside the palace. Ortaköy is very lively on weekends with street performers and food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the world's finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Then explore the ancient Theodosian Walls — the massive 5th-century fortifications that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — two of Istanbul's most historically rich and photogenic areas. Wander through colorful Ottoman-era houses, visit the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, and explore local art galleries and boutique cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in the Fener-Balat area at one of the trendy yet affordable restaurants that have opened in recent years in these revitalized historic neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Balat café — homemade Turkish food, soups, and fresh bread — budget 120–200 TRY.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Balat neighborhood restaurant — try contemporary takes on Ottoman recipes — budget 250–400 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Balat and Fener are extremely photogenic — bring your camera. The colorful staircases and painted houses are iconic. These neighborhoods are undergoing gentrification but remain authentic. Wear comfortable shoes for hilly cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum with rotating exhibitions and a permanent collection of 20th and 21st-century Turkish art. Great café with Bosphorus views inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — featuring the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting by Osman Hamdi Bey, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. Then browse the antique shops and galleries of Çukurcuma — Istanbul's antiques district.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — a UNESCO-recognized Sufi ritual performed at venues such as the Hodjapasha Cultural Center in Sirkeci. A deeply spiritual and mesmerizing cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Istanbul Modern café — enjoy a light meal with stunning Bosphorus views — budget 200–300 TRY.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner near Sirkeci — try a traditional Ottoman cuisine restaurant — budget 300–450 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern entry is approximately 200–300 TRY. Pera Museum entry is around 150–200 TRY. The Whirling Dervishes ceremony at Hodjapasha costs approximately 400–600 TRY — book tickets online in advance as shows sell out.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a short ferry ride from Kabataş or Bostancı. Visit Büyükada (the largest island) — a car-free island with Victorian mansions, pine forests, and horse-drawn carriages. Rent a bicycle and explore at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — hike up to the hilltop Aya Yorgi Monastery for panoramic views of the Sea of Marmara. Relax on the island's small beaches or in a waterfront café. The islands have a timeless, peaceful atmosphere far from the city bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon. Enjoy a final special dinner in Sultanahmet or Beyoğlu — treat yourself to a memorable meal at a restaurant you've been eyeing during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early — ferry departs from Kabataş around 9:00–10:00 AM).
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — fresh calamari, sea bream, and salad — budget 300–450 TRY per person.
meals.dinner: Special farewell-style dinner at a top-rated mid-range Istanbul restaurant — try classic Ottoman dishes or a tasting menu — budget 500–700 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets to the Princes' Islands cost approximately 50–80 TRY each way using an Istanbulkart. Bicycle rentals on the island are around 100–150 TRY per hour. The islands are very popular on weekends — consider visiting on a weekday if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit a favorite neighborhood or spot you didn't get enough of. Consider a quiet morning at a traditional Turkish café sipping çay and reading, or pick up last-minute gifts at the Arasta Bazaar near Sultanahmet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure time, visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an atmospheric underground Byzantine cistern with 336 marble columns and atmospheric lighting — a quick but unforgettable visit.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Istanbul Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and the long terminal walk at Istanbul's massive new airport.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast at the hotel — savor every bite of the cheeses, olives, and fresh bread.
meals.lunch: Quick but quality lunch near Sultanahmet — try a classic Turkish soup and gözleme — budget 100–150 TRY.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport if time allows, or grab a final simit and Turkish coffee before boarding.

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern entry is approximately 300–400 TRY — it has been renovated and is stunning. Check out time is typically 12:00 PM — ask the hotel about luggage storage if needed. Keep some TRY for airport expenses. Istanbul's new airport (IST) is massive — allow extra time for navigation.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in, unwind with a welcome amenity and late-night room service.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — request the chef's selection of mezze, grilled seafood, and Turkish desserts paired with local wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private meet-and-greet airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in luggage storage if needed. Keep the evening light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the Bosphorus. Afterward, take a private guided orientation walk along the Beachfront promenade to acclimate to Istanbul's coastal atmosphere and enjoy panoramic sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a private Bosphorus yacht cruise — sail past Dolmabahçe Palace, the Rumeli Fortress, and the iconic suspension bridges. Enjoy champagne and seasonal canapés on deck while your guide narrates the city's layered history from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop bar, then dinner at a premier waterfront restaurant in Kuruçeşme or Bebek — renowned for fresh seafood and stunning Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: À la carte terrace breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh pastries, sucuk eggs, kaymak with honey, seasonal fruits, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Light mezze and grilled fish served on the yacht during the cruise
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lacivert Restaurant (Anadoluhisarı) or Poseidon (Bebek) — whole sea bass, lobster, and fine Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht cruise at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge. Sunscreen and a light layer recommended for the boat. May weather in Istanbul is mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Topkapı Palace — explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Spoonmaker's Diamond and Topkapı Dagger), the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics of the Palace's inner sanctum. Skip-the-line VIP access included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the adjacent Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque for an in-depth private tour of its Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and centuries of layered history. Continue to the nearby Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque) to admire its iconic six minarets and İznik tile interior.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the atmospheric Sultanahmet neighborhood at dusk, then enjoy a classical Ottoman dinner experience in a restored historic mansion.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Private lunch at Matbah Restaurant inside the Ottoman Imperial Cuisine tradition — stuffed lamb, saffron pilaf, and rose sherbet
meals.dinner: Dinner at Seasons Restaurant (Four Seasons Sultanahmet) — refined Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus-view terrace

day_by_day.notes: Women should carry a scarf for mosque visits. Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays — confirm schedule. Private guide highly recommended for full historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Basilica Cistern — marvel at the ancient underground Byzantine reservoir with its forest of 336 columns and mysterious Medusa heads. Newly renovated with immersive lighting. Follow with a visit to the Istanbul Archaeology Museums — three world-class museums housing the Alexander Sarcophagus and ancient Near Eastern artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) with a personal luxury shopping guide — discover fine handwoven kilims, Ottoman antiques, 22-karat gold jewelry, and hand-painted ceramics. Access curated artisan workshops off the tourist path.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private traditional Turkish hammam ritual at Çemberlitaş Hamamı (1584) or the exclusive Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı — full scrub, foam massage, and oil treatment in a historic domed setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hafız Mustafa 1864 in Sultanahmet — börek, lentil soup, and Ottoman sweets
meals.dinner: Dinner at Neolokal (SALT Galata) — contemporary Anatolian cuisine with a tasting menu highlighting heirloom Turkish ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session in advance, especially for private suite options. The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays — this is a Saturday visit, so it will be open. Comfortable walking shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü — sample exotic spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and artisan cheeses. Then cross the Golden Horn to explore the historic Süleymaniye Mosque, masterpiece of architect Mimar Sinan, with sweeping views over the old city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historic districts. Walk through rainbow-painted streets, visit the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, and browse independent art galleries and antique shops. Private guide provides deep cultural and architectural context.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Beyoğlu with panoramic Golden Horn views, followed by dinner in the vibrant Karaköy district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Authentic local lunch at a family-run meyhane in Balat — homemade dolma, liver (arnavut ciğeri), and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Karaköy Lokantası — celebrated for its seasonal Ottoman-inspired menu and excellent wine list

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — Balat's cobblestone streets are uneven. This neighborhood is one of Istanbul's most photogenic; bring a camera. The area is best explored slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a private speedboat from the Beachfront to Büyükada, the largest island. Explore by horse-drawn carriage or bicycle, visit the historic Greek Orthodox Monastery of St. George on the hilltop, and enjoy the island's Belle Époque wooden mansions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on a secluded beach or cove on Büyükada. Swim in the clear Marmara Sea, sunbathe, and enjoy the car-free tranquility of the island. Optional kayaking or paddleboarding available.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat at sunset. Dinner at the resort or at a nearby Beachfront seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet picnic breakfast prepared by the resort for the boat journey
meals.lunch: Lunch at Milady's Restaurant on Büyükada — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and cold mezze with Aegean wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — fresh catch of the day with local herbs and Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Private speedboat is significantly faster than the public ferry (20 min vs. 90 min). Book in advance. No motorized vehicles are permitted on the island — embrace the peaceful pace.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the European Bosphorus shore. Tour the Crystal Staircase, the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier (the world's largest), and the ceremonial halls where Atatürk spent his final days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı district — Istanbul's answer to Mayfair or the Marais. Browse flagship boutiques of Turkish designers (Vakko, Beymen), international luxury brands, and stylish concept stores. Enjoy a leisurely café stop at a chic patisserie.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony at a historic tekke or cultural center — an intimate, deeply spiritual Sufi ritual experience arranged exclusively for small groups.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sunset Grill & Bar (Ulus) — modern Turkish and international cuisine with panoramic Bosphorus views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mikla Restaurant (The Marmara Pera rooftop) — celebrated chef Mehmet Gürs's modern Nordic-Anatolian tasting menu with extraordinary city views

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — confirm schedule. Photography is restricted inside the palace. The Sema ceremony is a respectful cultural experience, not a tourist show — dress modestly.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a celebrated Istanbul chef — learn to prepare classic Ottoman and Turkish dishes: börek, imam bayıldı, lamb stew, and baklava. Visit a local market beforehand to select fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — home to Osman Hamdi Bey's iconic 'The Tortoise Trainer' and exceptional collections of Orientalist paintings and Anatolian weights and measures. Stroll the historic Grande Rue de Péra (İstiklal Caddesi) and ride the antique Tünel funicular.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Cihangir neighborhood — a bohemian enclave of independent cafés, galleries, and wine bars beloved by Istanbul's creative class. Enjoy a relaxed evening in one of its atmospheric meyhanes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as a private lunch with your chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuma (Cihangir) or Antiochia — southeastern Anatolian cuisine featuring dishes from Antakya, with pomegranate molasses, walnut sauces, and slow-cooked meats

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class can be arranged through the concierge with a private chef for a fully personalized experience. İstiklal Caddesi is extremely busy on weekends — embrace the energy or visit early afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Edirne (2.5 hours by private car) — visit the magnificent Selimiye Mosque, Mimar Sinan's own masterpiece which he considered superior to Hagia Sophia. Explore the historic city center, the old bazaar district, and the Muradiye Mosque complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Edirne: visit the Kırkpınar Oil Wrestling Museum (home of the world's oldest sporting event), the Rüstem Pasha Caravanserai, and sample the city's famous liver (ciğer) cuisine before the return drive.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul and resort. Relaxed evening with spa treatment at the resort's wellness center — choose from a range of massage therapies and hydrotherapy options.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Edirne at a traditional lokanta — Edirne-style liver (tava ciğeri), white cheese, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort's terrace — mezze spread and grilled fish with local wine

day_by_day.notes: Private car with driver-guide is essential for Edirne. The round trip is approximately 5 hours driving total — an early start (7:30 AM) is recommended. Edirne is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) — home to the most magnificent Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, recently reopened after restoration. Then explore the ancient Theodosian Land Walls of Constantinople, a UNESCO World Heritage Site stretching 6.5 km across the old city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most sacred Islamic sites, rarely visited by tourists. Take the historic Pierre Loti cable car up to the hilltop café for sweeping Golden Horn views, where the French novelist famously wrote.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Beyoğlu for a curated Istanbul street food tour — guided tasting walk through Karaköy and Galata sampling simit, kokoreç, midye dolma (stuffed mussels), Turkish ice cream, and fresh pomegranate juice.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Asitane Restaurant (Kariye Hotel) — specializing in recreated Ottoman palace recipes from archival sources, a truly unique culinary experience
meals.dinner: Street food tour serves as the evening meal — curated premium version with private guide

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church may have restricted photography — confirm upon arrival. Eyüp Sultan is an active place of worship; dress modestly and respectfully. The street food tour is best arranged through a specialist local guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — one of Turkey's finest private art museums, housing Ottoman miniatures, calligraphy, clocks, and a world-class collection of Çanakkale ceramics. Stroll through the adjacent Emirgan Park, famous for its tulip gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asian side of Istanbul — cross the Bosphorus by private water taxi to Kadıköy. Wander through the vibrant Kadıköy Market, the Moda neighborhood's charming streets, and the Yeldeğirmeni street art district. Browse independent bookshops and design stores.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Kadıköy, then dinner at one of the Asian side's acclaimed restaurants before returning to the resort by private water taxi.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a celebrated Kadıköy fish market restaurant — fresh grilled mackerel sandwiches, calamari, and cold raki
meals.dinner: Dinner at Çiya Sofrası (Kadıköy) — legendary restaurant serving rare Anatolian regional dishes from across Turkey, a culinary institution

day_by_day.notes: Çiya Sofrası is world-famous and featured in international food guides — reservations essential. The Kadıköy market is best on weekday afternoons. Private water taxi is the most scenic and efficient way to cross.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private tour of the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (recently relocated to its stunning new Renzo Piano-designed waterfront building in Karaköy) — contemporary Turkish art, photography galleries, and permanent collection. Followed by a visit to the SALT Galata cultural center in the historic Ottoman Bank building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full afternoon of luxury at the resort's spa — choose from a signature hammam ritual, deep tissue massage, facial treatment, and time in the thermal pools. Completely unscheduled time for relaxation, reading, or a final swim in the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail experience: private rooftop terrace reservation at the resort or a celebrated Bosphorus-view venue for sunset champagne. Grand farewell dinner at one of Istanbul's most prestigious fine dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent champagne breakfast on your private balcony at the resort — fresh croissants, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, and seasonal fruits
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Istanbul Modern's waterfront café — artisan sandwiches, salads, and specialty coffee
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Tuğra Restaurant (Çırağan Palace Kempinski) — the pinnacle of Ottoman fine dining inside a 19th-century imperial palace on the Bosphorus

day_by_day.notes: Tuğra at Çırağan Palace requires a dress code (smart elegant) and advance reservation. This is one of Istanbul's most iconic dining experiences — a fitting finale. Request a window table overlooking the Bosphorus.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the resort's terrace. Take a slow walk along the Beachfront promenade one final time, collect any last-minute gifts from nearby boutiques, and soak in the Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport. Depart Istanbul with extraordinary memories of one of the world's greatest cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure

meals.breakfast: Final grand Turkish breakfast spread at the resort — a celebration of 13 days of culinary discovery
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a quick stop at a quality café near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Istanbul Airport. The resort concierge can arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Request a late checkout (subject to availability) to maximize your final morning.
